title: Cap. X: Against Hosea — imputation follows; God not author of perdition
pass_a_gloss: Add this: if the true, solid, unique cause of that discrimination is God's will, to whom it so pleased to impute Adam's first sin to us all and not to impute Adam's later sins or other parents' sins, then one must confess (what conscience flees most fiercely) that the true, solid, unique cause why we are sinners and lost is God's will — against the oracle, 'From you is your destruction, O Israel.' Placeus does grant that with the propagation of original vice an imputation coheres, unless God's mercy intervenes — but that imputation follows propagation, does not precede it, and is in no way the cause of propagation. But to set an imputation by which Adam's actual sin becomes ours, by which we become sinners and liable to eternal death, which is to be the cause of sin's propagation, and to make God's will the unique cause of this imputation — what is that but to make God the author of our perdition, if this is not?
pass_b_english: There is more. If the true, solid, and only cause of that difference is God's will — pleased to charge Adam's first sin to us all, yet not pleased to charge Adam's later sins or the sins of other parents — then we must confess what conscience most fiercely flees: that the true, solid, and only cause of our being sinners and lost is God's will. That runs against the oracle, From you is your destruction, O Israel. I do admit that, where original vice propagates, an imputation hangs together with it unless mercy from God steps in; yet that imputation comes after the propagation, never before it, and never as its cause. But to plant an imputation that makes Adam's actual sin ours, that makes us sinners and debtors to eternal death, that is then treated as the cause of sin's spread, and whose only cause is said to be God's will — if that is not to cast God as the author of our perdition, what is?
source_text: Adde quod, si rei illius vera & solida, & unica causa est Dei voluntas, cui sic libuit nobis omnibus primum Adami peccatum imputare; nec libuit aut sequentia Adami, aut aliorum parentum peccata imputare, fatendum est (id quod vehementissime refugit conscientia) veram & solidam & unicam causam cur simus peccatores & perditi, Dei voluntatem esse, contra oraculum, Ex te perditio tua, o Israel. Fateor equidem cum propagatione vitii originalis imputationem, nisi Dei misericordia intercedat, cohaerere, sed ea imputatio sequitur propagationem, non antecedit, nec est ullo modo propagationis causa. At ponere imputationem, qua peccatum actuale Adami nostrum fiat, qua fiamus peccatores & rei mortis aeternae, quae sit causa propagationis peccati, & hujus imputationis unicam esse causam Dei voluntatem, quid est facere Deum perditionis nostrae autorem, si hoc non est?
